Washed
WAWSHT
adjective (Gen Alpha slang)
Short for washed up, an early-twentieth-century American expression (theater and sports) for a person whose career or powers are finished — like debris washed up on a beach. Gen-Z and Gen Alpha clipped it to washed: "he’s washed" means past his prime, no longer good, often said of older athletes, older siblings, and fathers trying a trick on the trampoline. It sits beside unc and fell off in the vocabulary of decline.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

To Gen Alpha, someone who is washed is past his prime — an old athlete, a grown-up who can’t do the things he used to, a big brother who lost at a video game. "Dad, you’re washed" is a common tease. The Christian observation: this is one of the words where Scripture simply takes the slang and turns it into the gospel. In the Bible, being washed is the best thing that can happen to a person. "Wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow" (Psa 51:7). Paul told a church full of former sinners, "such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus" (1Co 6:11). Christ is the One "that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood" (Rev 1:5), and He told Peter, "If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me" (Joh 13:8). As for the slang’s sense — past your prime — Scripture is kind to the aging: the righteous "shall still bring forth fruit in old age" (Psa 92:14). A father can tell a five-year-old: "People say ‘washed’ to mean old and not good anymore. But the Bible says being washed is wonderful — Jesus washes our hearts clean! Has Jesus washed you?" And he can laugh when his son calls him washed, and answer, "Yes — and so can you be."

Webster 1828 Definition

Clipped washed up (early 20th c.): past one’s prime — a tease at the aging that Scripture turns into the gospel’s best word, "ye are washed."

expand to see more

WASHED, a. (slang, from washed up; Gen-Z and Gen Alpha usage, 2010s–present) Past one’s prime; no longer skilled or relevant. "He used to be good at basketball, but now he’s washed."

Related: unc, fell off, cooked.

Decode for parents: affectionate teasing at home; occasionally a sneer at age.

Webster 1828, the root — WASH, v.t. To cleanse by ablution, or by rubbing in water; as, to wash the hands or the body; to wash garments.

Key Scripture

Psa 51:7 — "Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow."

1Co 6:11 — "And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God."

Rev 1:5 — "And from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood,"

Joh 13:8 — "Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me."

Psa 92:14 — "They shall still bring forth fruit in old age; they shall be fat and flourishing;"

Modern Corruption

"Washed" mocks the aging and the faded; Scripture honors the fruitful old and makes "washed" the word for every sinner cleansed by Christ.

expand to see more

The slang belongs to a youth culture that measures people by peak performance and treats decline as a joke. In small doses it is family teasing; as a habit it becomes contempt for age, which Scripture forbids: "Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man" (Lev 19:32).

Redeem it with delight. Few slang words hand a father such an easy gospel line. Let your child call you washed; tell him what washed means in the Bible; ask whether he has been washed by Christ. Then honor the old people in your family loudly, so that he learns age is a crown, not a punchline.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English wascan → wash → washed up (early 20th-c. theater and sports) → clipped washed (2010s).

Old English wascan — to wash

Early 20th c.: washed up, finished (of a career)

2010s: clipped to washed in sports and youth slang

Gen Alpha: "Dad, you’re washed"

Usage

""You can’t do a backflip anymore, Dad. You’re washed." "Washed in the blood, son.""

"But ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified (1Co 6:11)."

"They shall still bring forth fruit in old age — not washed up (Psa 92:14)."
